end.summary:
Pihu identified that earthworms live in soil and named ants, beetles, and millipedes as soil animals.
They discussed that tunnels can let air and water into soil.
They identified dead leaves as material soil animals help break down.
The belief that earthworms spoil soil or eat crops remained after three attempts; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised how soil animals help by using questions about air, water, tunnels, and dead leaves. Pihu named several soil animals and connected tunnels with water entering soil. The mix-up that earthworms harm soil or crops was not corrected by the end of the lesson. At home, look at a picture or short book about earthworms and repeat: “Their tunnels let in air and water, and they help make rich soil.”
